catalog_quote: Stress in the Gilaki language is dynamic. In words not having inflectional, morphological endings, it falls on the last syllable: (12) a. xånə́ house b. kårəgə́r worker c. šenǻ swimming. In the situation where the case enclitic -ə of the genitive case, -a of the accusative case, or the “Ezafe” enclitic -ə joins to the noun, the stress remains on the stem: (13) a. mi pérə xånə my father’s house b. u duxtə́ra bavər bring this girl c. fíkrə Məryəm the thought of Maryam. In a verb in the forms of the aorist, the present-future tense and the imperative mood, the stress falls on the end of the word, that is, on the personal ending: (14) a. bəgə́m (if) I say b. kunə́m I am doing, I shall do c. bukún do! (singular) d. bukuníd do! (plural). In the presence of negation in the same forms the stress passes to the negative particle: (15) a. nə́-gəm I shall not say, I am not saying b. nə́-gə (if) he/she does not say c. nú-kunəm I am not doing, I shall not do d. nú-kun do not do! (singular) e. nú-kunid do not do! (plural). In the past neutral and past continuous tenses, the stress remains on the stem: (16) a. bəgóftə he/she said b. góftim I was saying
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Dynamic (expiratory) word stress on the final syllable of the uninflected word (stem-final); case and ezafe enclitics, the indefinite -i and the enclitic copula are outside the stress domain, so stress stays on the last stem syllable. Verbs are morphologically conditioned: personal endings carry stress in aorist/present-future/imperative, the negative prefix nV- always attracts stress, and past neutral/past continuous forms keep stress on the stem (not on bə- or the ending).
new_statements.exceptions: Enclitics (genitive -ə, accusative -a, ezafe -ə) unstressed; vocative use of nouns shifts stress to the first syllable (bə́rara 'O my brother'); negative particle stressed (nə́-gəm, nú-kun); past tenses stem-stressed (bəgóftə); enclitic copula unstressed but negative copula ní- stressed (p. 132). Stilo (EIr. 2001) adds lexical/morphological minimal pairs (xaná 'legible' vs xána 'the khan-OBJ', bídin 'see!' vs bidín 'irreligious') and notes Eastern Gilaki (Lahijani) has more initial-stressed verb forms, with bV- stressed in all tenses.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level; rule stated for citation forms of uninflected words, with morphological conditioning in inflected nouns and verbs. Description based on the speech of Rasht (Western Gilaki) informants.
new_statements.identity_note: Rastorgueva et al. describe the Gilaki of the city of Rasht (Western Gilaki, 'Rashti'), based on Rasht-born informants in Moscow and Rashti texts; Glottolog treats Rashti as a dialect under gila1241. Stilo (EIr.) notes that Eastern Gilaki (Lahijani) differs mainly in verb stress (more initial-stressed verb forms, bV- stressed in all tenses) while 'other stress rules are common to all dialects', so the final-stress rule for nouns/uninflected words holds language-wide.

tone_statements.citation: Ivanov, Vladimir B. & Liubov G. Silanteva. 2023. Research on word stress in Iranian languages by Soviet and Russian scholars [Issledovanie slovesnogo udarenija v iranskix jazykax sovetskimi i rossijskimi uchenymi]. Russian Journal of Linguistics 27(2): 392-417. Moscow: RUDN University. (Review article, text in English.)
tone_statements.quote: Previously word stress in Gilaki was described as purely dynamic (Rastorgueva et al. 2012: 19, 1971: 27, Rastorgueva 1999b: 115). In 2015 a further study was conducted on the Gilaki language. The speech of three men and one woman was recorded; 41 two-syllable words (82 syllables) with initial and final stress were analyzed. The experiment showed that word stress in Gilaki is two- componential – tonal-dynamic12. Pitch is a more reliable indicator in this process: on average it is 9.4% higher in the stressed syllable (Sig<0.001), while intensity rises only by 2.3% (Sig=0.006).
tone_statements.locator: p. 403, sec. 4.4 'Gilaki' ('12' after 'tonal-dynamic' is footnote call 12, citing Ivanov 2015 'Gilyakskaya prosodiya', pp. 86-87)

tone_statements.quote: Согласно слуховым оценкам ударение в ГЯ однокомпонентное динамическое (Расторгуева, 1999) с. 115, (Расторгуева, и др., 1971) с. 27. Переопределяя их, отметим, что ударение в ГЯ – двухкомпонентное, тоно-динамическое. Основным фактором является тон, второстепенным – интенсивность.
tone_statements.translation: According to auditory assessments, stress in Gilaki is single-component, dynamic (Rastorgueva 1999: 115; Rastorgueva et al. 1971: 27). Redefining these, we note that stress in Gilaki is two-component, tono-dynamic. The main factor is tone [F0], the secondary one intensity.

tone_statements.quote: 2.1.2. Ударение в Г.я. динамическое; как правило, падает на последний слог слова: xånə́ 'дом', xarbəzə́ 'дыня', dirúz 'вчера'. С присоединением словообразующих суффиксов ударение переносится на них: čål 'яма' — čåləká 'ямочка, углубление', ǰəvån 'юноша, парень' — ǰəvånák 'паренек'. Не принимают на себя ударения: 1) падежные показатели -ə (род. п.), -a (вин. п.) ... 2) изафетный показатель -ə ...
tone_statements.translation: 2.1.2. Stress in Gilaki is dynamic; as a rule it falls on the last syllable of the word: xånə́ 'house', xarbəzə́ 'melon', dirúz 'yesterday'. When derivational suffixes are added the stress moves onto them: čål 'pit' — čåləká 'small pit, hollow', ǰəvån 'youth, lad' — ǰəvånák 'laddie'. The following do not take stress: 1) the case markers -ə (gen.), -a (acc.) ... 2) the ezafe marker -ə ...
tone_statements.summary: The only word-prosodic statement in the 14-page sketch: the accent is 'dynamic' (Russian term for intensity stress as opposed to musical/pitch accent), word-final with morphological exceptions; tone or pitch nowhere mentioned. 'No tone' is coded from that term, hence medium confidence.

sources.note: Section 2.4 'Stress', p. 19: stress is dynamic; in words without inflectional endings it falls on the last syllable (xåne´, kårəgə´r, šenå´); case/ezafe enclitics (-ə, -a) do not take stress (stress stays on stem); aorist/present-future/imperative verbs stress the personal ending; negative particle nə-/nu-/ni- attracts stress; past neutral and past continuous keep stress on the stem (bəgóftə, góftim). Elsewhere: vocative nouns shift stress to the first syllable (p. ~65); enclitic copula unstressed, negative copula stressed on ní- (p. 132).

sources.citation: Stilo, Donald. 2001. GILAN x. Languages. Encyclopaedia Iranica, Vol. X, Fasc. 6, pp. 660-668 (online edition, last updated 25 Nov 2013).
sources.note: Paragraph 'Stress.': 'Stress is mostly syllable-final, but some morphemes, particularly in verb forms, require stress shifts' (xayə´m 'I want', nə´xayəm 'I don't want', bəxástidi..); more Eastern Gilaki verb forms take initial stress than Western Gilaki; negation nV´- obligatorily stressed; WG bV- stressed in subjunctive/imperative, unstressed in past/perfect; EG bV- stressed in all forms; lists minimal stress contrasts (xaná 'legible' vs xána 'the khan (obj.)', ruzí vs rúzi, bídin 'see!' vs bidín 'irreligious'); indefinite -i and object marker -(y)a/-ra unstressed.

sources.note: Says nothing about stress placement, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the catalog's final-stress record (Rastorgueva et al. 2012, sec. 2.4, p. 19).
